title: IBM Opens Its 0.7nm Nanostack Process To Chip Designers In Q1 2027, Shipping Design Kits For Tech That Could Be The Next Breakthrough For Reducing AI Chip Size
key_facts: IBM announced plans to make an early research and development process design kit (PDK) for its 7-angstrom (0.7 nm) nanostack technology available in the first quarter of 2027.

Nanostack stacks n-type and p-type transistors one above the other instead of side by side; IBM says it gives nearly 100 billion transistors on a 150 mm2 chip, almost double the density of its 2 nm node, 50 percent better performance, 70 percent more energy efficiency and 40 percent SRAM scaling.
A PDK provides the models, design rules and libraries engineers need to start designing chips for a process.
Potential collaborators: fabless chip companies, design-software (EDA) vendors, equipment suppliers and research organisations.
The first PDK will include example standard-cell libraries and an example SRAM design, but not every model of a mature commercial kit.
IBM Research's post is dated 13 Oct 2026 (Google News); Wccftech's article is dated 16 Oct 2026 and says the technology was launched in June (IBM says 'earlier this year').
Wccftech adds that SRAM is about 10 percent of die area in Nvidia's H100 and 12 to 15 percent with L1 cache.
quote_evidence: IBM is announcing plans to make available an early research and development process design kit, or PDK, for the 7-angstrom nanostack technology in the first quarter of 2027.
The initial release will not contain every model that a mature commercial PDK would include.
IBM’s planned offering will help semiconductor companies evaluate nanostack technology well before it is ready for widespread adoption.
why_it_matters_hint: An early research kit lets chip firms and tool makers start preparing for a stacked-transistor layout.
notes: Event is 13 Oct 2026 (IBM Research post), older than the window; Wccftech ran it on 16 Oct. Wccftech's headline ('opens its process to chip designers') overstates an early research kit.
